response.summary: The revision resolves the first-round findings F1 to F6 at plan level: owner and Google email pinning, a separate owner-bound ticket table, chunked cursors, exact-email matching, source-only upsert with revisioned RPCs, and strict Docs URL parsing. I found three new defects in the revised text: a cursor race, missing Calendar list parameters, and a conflict between worker and manual transcript writes. The plan is not yet implementation-safe on these points. I verified nothing against source, because no implementation exists yet.

findings.evidence: The plan has no run lock or monotonic cursor rule. If a cron tick overlaps a slow run, or a retry and a scheduled call both hold valid tickets, both runs scan the same chunk. A run finishing late can then write an older chunk end over a newer covered_through. The next run rescans harmlessly, but a stale writer can also overwrite last-error or last-success state and mislead the Home status. A rewind past the cutoff is also possible if the write is not guarded.
findings.fix: Take a per-owner advisory lock or a lease row at the start of each run, and return 'busy' if it is held. Advance the cursor with a compare-and-set: UPDATE ... SET covered_through = :new WHERE covered_through = :expected AND :new > covered_through. Never move the cursor backwards. Add a test for two concurrent runs.

findings.evidence: The plan relies on recurring instance IDs and on cancelled events, but it does not require the list parameters that make them appear. Without singleEvents=true, recurring series return as one master event and instance IDs are not produced. Without showDeleted=true, cancelled events are omitted from the list, so cancellations are only found through the 20-task revisit. A 24-hour overlap also misses events created or edited later that ended earlier than 24 hours ago, such as a session added after the fact or an attachment added days later, until the revisit rotation reaches them (which only covers existing unhandled tasks).
findings.fix: Specify singleEvents=true, showDeleted=true, orderBy=startTime and maxResults paging for the scan. Add a second pass with updatedMin set to the last successful run time, so late-created or late-edited events inside the covered range are found. Test a recurring series, a cancelled instance and a late-created event.

findings.evidence: The source-only upsert includes the transcript Doc ID, because it is derived from the Calendar attachment. The teacher can also attach a Doc explicitly. The plan does not say which wins. A later resync that finds no attachment, or a different one, can silently overwrite or clear the teacher's manual link. Two attachment candidates arriving later can also flip an auto-linked task back to needs review.
findings.fix: Store the transcript source as 'auto' or 'manual'. The worker may write transcript fields only when the source is not 'manual'. Manual changes go through a revisioned RPC and are recorded in the task-event history. Test that a resync after a manual attach leaves the manual link in place.

coverage: Host dispositions for the first-round findings F1 to F6.
Calendar scan, cursor, ticket and transcript semantics checked against the plan only.
Round-1 reading of googleCalendar.ts and the existing ticket callers, carried forward.
limitations: No implementation exists, so nothing was checked against source.
I did not inspect the Drive copy tooling in the vault, which is outside this checkout.
I did not run tests or previews.
The existing booking ticket RPC definition is absent from this repository's migrations, so it remains unverified. The revised plan avoids it.
